cylinder_sdf — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: coordgrid → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.cylinder_sdf(grid, center, axis, radius, height) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.cylinder_sdf(grid, center, axis, radius, height); from the registry, ops3d.get("cylinder_sdf"))

Usage

Exact signed distance field of a finite-length cylinder (flat caps at both ends) (negative inside, positive outside).

Split into the axial distance t and the radius from the axis r, set q = (r - radius, |t| - height/2), and take outside = ‖max(q, 0)‖, inside = min(max(q), 0), sdf = outside + inside. This applies the same Quilez-style construction as box_sdf to "the 2-D cross-section (radius, axis)", so it is the true Euclidean distance to the side, the caps and the corners (rims) alike.

Arguments and validation (ValueError):

• grid: float array (..., 3) whose last axis is 3.

• center: the center of the cylinder (the centroid, not an end face; 3 elements).

• axis: axis direction (3 elements, zero vector and NaN are rejected; length is normalised automatically).

• radius: scalar equivalent to radius > 0 (0 is the axis line itself, negative is rejected).

• height: scalar full length (±height/2 from center; negative is rejected).

Returns: float64 of shape grid.shape[:-1].

Where to use: a through hole is sdf_subtract(part, cylinder_sdf(...)) (make height longer than the part so no rim of the end face remains). Bosses, pins and shafts use sdf_union. If you need an infinitely long cylinder, take height large enough (once the end faces are outside the evaluation domain, only the side matters).
